sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell in Seguin?
sections.html:
A cash sale to a buyer who takes the house as is tends to finish soonest, because no lender, appraisal or repair list slows it down. A listing can pay more, yet it means prep, showings and waiting on someone else's financing.

Seguin is the Guadalupe County seat. The Texas State Historical Association places it on Interstate 10 and the Guadalupe River, about 35 miles northeast of San Antonio. That position draws local buyers and people commuting toward San Antonio.

Decide first which goal ranks highest: a fixed closing date, a clean exit from a house with problems, or the top price. Each goal favors a different sale method.

sections.h2: What shaped Seguin and its housing stock?
sections.html:
Seguin was laid out in 1838 as Walnut Springs and renamed in February 1839. It was incorporated on February 7, 1853, according to the Handbook of Texas, and it already had a school chartered in 1849. The Handbook says that schoolhouse was recognized by the state in 1962 as the oldest continuously used school building in Texas.

Older parts of town therefore include homes with a long history, and the Handbook mentions antebellum houses including the Sebastopol House State Historic Structure. Houses of that age tend to need roof, wiring or plumbing work, which a buyer will price in.

The local economy started in agriculture and trade, took a lift when oil was found in the Darst Creek fields in the late 1920s, and later added manufacturing and services. Texas Lutheran University, which moved to a farm near Seguin in 1912, adds a campus to the mix.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and school district cover Seguin?
sections.html:
Guadalupe Appraisal District values property here, and its main office is in Seguin. Its member list includes the City of Seguin and Seguin ISD, which is the district most Seguin buyers will ask about.

The district runs an Appraisal Review Board that hears appeals, and a taxpayer liaison officer is on site on hearing days. Its site now offers online tools for homestead, disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, and printable forms remain available.

Who handles what for a Seguin parcel (Guadalupe Appraisal District and Texas Comptroller)

A mailing note from the district advises taking time sensitive mail to a post office counter for a manual postmark, since USPS processing changes in Texas can move the postmark date.

sections.h2: What else shaped Seguin's economy and neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Seguin's first economy was farming and trade. German emigrants passing from Indianola to the Hill Country brought better methods, and by the Civil War local farms grew cotton, corn and peanuts and raised hogs and cattle. Oil from the Darst Creek fields, fifteen miles east, lifted the town in the late 1920s.

The city changed from a mayor-council to a council-manager form of government in 1986. By 1988 it had an estimated 22,000 residents, and the Handbook records 22,011 residents and 1,338 businesses in 2000. Attractions include Max Starcke Park, the Guadalupe County Coliseum and fairgrounds, where the Texas State High School Rodeo has run since 1984.

Education runs through town too. Texas Lutheran University moved to the Louis Fritz Farm near Seguin in 1912 and took its present name in 1996, and Ball High School carries a name given in 1925 to the former Abraham Lincoln School. Mention nearby parks, campuses and schools when you describe the house, because buyers weigh them.

sections.h2: What permits does the City of Seguin require?
sections.html:
Seguin requires a permit to build, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, roof or re-roof a structure, or to put in a fence. Its list of work that needs no permit includes painting, siding, window replacement in an existing single-family home or duplex, fences under seven feet and roofing above the deck.

The city lets a person who owns and lives in a homestead do the work personally with the proper permits, but the house must be registered as a homestead with the Guadalupe appraisal district. Hired work must go through a contractor registered with the city.

For a one or two family home, the approved final inspection report is the certificate of occupancy, and the city issues no separate paper. Call the permits office at 830-401-2435 if you are unsure whether past work was permitted. Seguin has adopted the 2021 International Residential Code and a Unified Development Code, plus a flood ordinance that follows FEMA guidance.

sections.h2: How do taxes and deeds work for a Seguin sale?
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1 and bills come in October. Most owners must pay by January 31, and charges start the next day, February 1.

Deeds for Guadalupe County land go to the county clerk, after a notary or similar officer has witnessed the signature. The Texas courts manual puts page one at $5.00 and each added page at $4.00, so ask the clerk for the current total.

  • Warranty and quitclaim deeds are filed with the county clerk.
  • A trustee's deed comes after a foreclosure auction.
  • Unpaid taxes can attach to the house, and clear title waits until they are paid.
  • Ask the title company for a payoff figure before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What exemptions and caps should a Seguin seller know about?
sections.html:
A homestead appraisal cannot rise more than 10 percent a year, starting the year after the owner first qualifies. Owners 65 or older or disabled also get a school tax ceiling fixed at the amount paid in the year they qualified.

Disabled veterans receive exemptions by rating, starting at up to $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating and reaching up to $12,000 at 70 percent or higher. A 100 percent rating can mean a total exemption on the homestead.

Guadalupe Appraisal District offers online tools for these exemptions, and the general deadline is before May 1. Anyone who buys after January 1 may ask for the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller never held one. Heirs who are not on a recorded deed must give the district an affidavit of ownership interest plus the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, rented or in poor shape?
sections.html:
Inherited houses need the right paperwork first. Probate of a will is available for four years after death, and a muniment of title can pass a house when the estate owes nothing beyond real estate liens. A small estate affidavit may fit a smaller estate with no will, and it requires two disinterested witnesses and court approval.

A tenant can stay through a sale. If you want the house vacant instead, a landlord gives written notice and files in justice court, so selling with the tenant in place avoids the delay and the lease then goes with the house.

A house with deferred repairs is the simplest case: a buyer who takes it as is handles the work and you skip contractor bids.

faqs.a: The Guadalupe Appraisal District, whose office is in Seguin. Its member list includes the City of Seguin and Seguin ISD.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for Seguin window replacement?
faqs.a: Not for an existing single-family home or duplex, according to the city's no permit list. Roof work above the deck and painting are also on that list, but ask the permits office at 830-401-2435 when in doubt.

faqs.q: Is there a certificate of occupancy for a Seguin house?
faqs.a: For one and two family homes, the approved final inspection report acts as the certificate, and the city issues no separate document.

faqs.q: When must Seguin property tax be paid?
faqs.a: Most owners pay by January 31. A bill still open on February 1 is delinquent and picks up penalty and interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Seguin house that is in probate?
faqs.a: Often yes, once the court has named someone with authority or the title has passed by muniment or affidavit. Ask a title company which path applies to your estate.
